diagnostics.message: :resource.aws_lambda_function.main depends only on :resource.aws_iam_role.main and vars, so nothing orders its creation after :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role. When vpc_config is enabled (var.lambda.subnet_ids/security_group_ids set), the function can exist while the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy is still unattached; any invocation before that lands (mid-apply or after a partial apply) fails because the execution role cannot create network interfaces. The provider docs show the function with depends_on the role policy attachment ("Ensure IAM role and log group are ready"). No attribute reference expresses this ordering, so a bare depends_on is required.

:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging is only created after :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main, which is itself created after :resource.aws_lambda_function.main (the log group name references the function), so the function always exists before its inline logging policy is attached. Early invocations run with a role lacking logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents permissions; the provider docs recommend the function depend on its logging policy/log group. No attribute reference on the function can express this, so a bare depends_on is needed - but see the missing function->log_group ordering: the log group's name must first be decoupled from aws_lambda_function.main.function_name to avoid a dependency cycle.

When var.lambda.tracing_config.mode is set, :resource.aws_lambda_function.main is created with tracing mode Active, but nothing orders it after :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray, so the xray:PutTraceSegments/xray:PutTelemetryRecords permissions may be attached only once the function already exists and early invocations cannot deliver traces. This is the same operational readiness ordering the provider docs illustrate with depends_on on the role's policies; no attribute reference expresses it, so a bare depends_on is required.

Operationally :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main must exist before :resource.aws_lambda_function.main (the provider docs show the function with "Ensure log group exists before function" via depends_on), but the graph only has the reverse edge: the log group's name is derived from aws_lambda_function.main.function_name, forcing the function to be created first. In that window, an invocation (external trigger mid-apply, or after a partial apply) makes Lambda auto-creates the log group without the configured retention/KMS settings, and the subsequent aws_cloudwatch_log_group create then fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group name is fully derivable from var.lambda.prefix/var.lambda.name, so that coupling should be dropped and the function should depend on the log group instead; a bare depends_on on the function expresses the ordering once the name reference is removed.
